name: nanoGPT-shakespeare-char
notes: Ran as published — zero patches. Two commands, three real dependencies, 10.65M parameters, 2.5 minutes on one GPU. Best validation loss 1.4666 against the README's quoted 1.4697, on a script that sets no seed. prepare.py's four printed dataset statistics matched the expected values it records in its own source exactly. Only deviation is --compile=False, a flag the README itself documents, which drops a host-specific compile warm-up with no payoff at this scale. Findings are all documentation-level: the README's install line omits requests (needed by the very first quick-start command) while listing four packages this recipe never imports; the corpus is fetched from an unpinned master-branch URL; and prepare.py writes its generated data into the source tree with no way to redirect it, so the data directory is an output directory and must be treated as one or the prepare-to-train chain is lost. The one change worth making upstream is small: write the eval history to CSV/JSONL in out_dir unconditionally, so every reproducer gets a durable learning curve without a wandb account.
